text:
denise: quick one — sample app fails on Fresh/Deno during import: `Error: Package subpath './runtime' is not defined by "exports"` when doing `import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-inference'`. Works fine in Node with bundlers. anyone seen this with conditional exports + types combo?

alex: yup. Deno (and some edge/runtimes) treat npm packages differently. Node resolves `exports` with conditions like "import"/"require", but Deno historically expects plain ESM entry files (with extensions) or an explicit deno-friendly entry.

sam: can you paste your package.json exports snippet?

denise: sure — current package.json (simplified):
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  },
  "./runtime": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/runtime/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/runtime/index.js"
  }
},
"types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
```

maria: couple of quick notes: 1) `types` is a top-level field and not a condition inside `exports` (so keep it at root). 2) TypeScript/TS Server and Deno will follow different resolution rules — Deno might not look at `exports` the same way Node + bundlers do, and it usually wants explicit .js imports (or an import_map).

alex: also watch out for pathless subpath imports. If a consumer does `import { x } from 'redwood-inference/runtime'`, Node can map via `exports` but Deno might not unless the package is published with a deno-ready entry (like `deno/mod.js` or a top-level `mod.js` with .js extensions).

sam: so what's the pragmatic fix? publish a small deno/edge entry that re-exports the ESM files with .js extensions?

maria: yes — two patterns we've used elsewhere:
1) Publish an extra `dist/deno/mod.js` (ESM w/ .js extensions) and add a visible entrypoint path like `import "redwood-inference/deno"` in docs.
2) Keep the Node `exports` map as-is for `import`/`require`, but add explicit subpath exports e.g. `"./deno": "./dist/deno/mod.js"` so Deno users can import `redwood-inference/deno`.

alex: small example export map suggestion: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" },
  "./runtime": { "import": "./dist/esm/runtime/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/runtime/index.js" },
  "./deno": "./dist/deno/mod.js"
}
```
This keeps Node niceties while giving Deno a simple path to import.

denise: that sounds doable. one more wrinkle: auth/retry code uses `node-fetch` + `AbortController` polyfills and retries using `setTimeout` + `clearTimeout`. On edge runtimes fetch is global and timers behave slightly differently — we saw token-refresh hanging in the sample app.

sam: yeah — recommend shipping a runtime abstraction layer (we already have a tiny one) but make it choose implementations at build time for `deno` vs `node` so the deno build bundles a fetch-native auth flow (no node-fetch), and timers use `globalThis.setTimeout` exclusively.

maria: and for typings: ensure d.ts references are published at the package root (via `types` top-level) and that generated `.d.ts` files use path imports that match the deno build if we expect users to import `.../deno`. Otherwise TS + Deno tooling will miss types.

alex: CI note: we should add a Fast-Integration test in GH actions that runs the sample app in a Deno container (e.g., deno run --reload) to catch these regressions early.

ci-bot: created issue #3412: "deno/edge: add deno build + deno entrypoint, ensure auth/retry runtime compatibility, update exports map and types" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/3412 :white_check_mark:

denise: sweet. plan for a tiny PR: 1) add `dist/deno` build with ESM + .js extensions, 2) add `"./deno"` export, 3) adjust auth runtime adapter for fetch-native, 4) add deno sample to examples/, 5) CI deno smoke test. i'll draft it today.

maria: one more nit — document the recommended import for deno users in the README and examples: `import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-inference/deno'` to avoid ambiguous subpath imports.

denise: noted. thanks everyone :sparkles:

alex: thanks — this will also reduce our support churn for edge users. :+1:
